name: 3725-woocommerce-payments-12089

pr.title: Fix express checkout crash when a wallet button is tapped mid-refresh
pr.body:
Fixes WOOPMNT-6265

#### Changes proposed in this Pull Request

On classic cart and checkout pages, WooCommerce refreshes the cart while the Express Checkout Element it already mounted stays clickable. A tap in that window ran the click handler against cleared cart data and threw while reading `shippingRates`, so the wallet never opened and the tap was never tracked.

The refresh window is now guarded on both fronts:

- A wallet tap during a refresh is rejected with `event.reject()`, and the button carries the same white overlay WooCommerce paints over the order review, so the shopper can see why the tap did nothing. The overlay alone is not enough: an element-level blockUI block intercepts pointers but not keyboard or screen-reader activation.
- On classic checkout the guard starts at `update_checkout`, before WooCommerce's own `update_order_review` request, because our button sits outside the area core greys out. Checkout only: the order-pay page fires `update_checkout` without a matching `updated_checkout`, so a guard raised there would never come down.
- Only the newest refresh may publish cart data or mount Elements. An older refresh that lands late is discarded, and it cannot lift the overlay from under the newer one.
- A refresh that fails clears the cached cart, which hides the button until a later healthy refresh restores it. A tap with no cart or product data is rejected instead of throwing.

The trade-off is that a shopper who taps during a refresh must tap again once it completes. Blocks cart and checkout are unaffected because they read the WooCommerce data store rather than this shortcode cache.

Covered by Jest: rejection during a refresh, the overlay lifecycle, superseded refreshes, failed refreshes, missing data, and the order-pay scoping (34 suites, 249 tests). The overlay and guard lifecycle was also checked in a browser on classic checkout, classic cart, product, and order-pay pages against real WooCommerce refreshes. On a test site with real wallet buttons, a Google Pay activation while WooCommerce's own request was pending, and again while the Store API cart request was pending, was rejected by the click handler with the overlay up; the same activation resolved normally once the refresh settled. A wallet payment completed after such a refresh was verified manually on that site.

**Backward compatibility:** The new `init()` arguments are optional and `init()` is internal to the bundle. `expressCheckoutButtonUi` gains an `unblock()` method and `unblockButton()` keeps its behavior. No public PHP APIs, hooks, filters, script handles, REST routes, options, or stored-data shapes change.

Bug introduced in PR #10784 and latent since 10.0.0.

#### Testing instructions

1. Enable Apple Pay or Google Pay and select a **classic shortcode checkout** page. Add a shippable product, open checkout, and wait for the wallet button.
2. In DevTools, enable the 3G throttling preset (called Slow 3G in older Chrome) and change the shipping country. While either the `update_order_review` or the `wc/store/v1/cart` request is pending, the wallet button is greyed out. Tap it anyway.
   - On `develop`, a tap during WooCommerce's request opens the sheet with the pre-change totals, and a tap during the cart request stays closed while the console reports an undefined `shippingRates` access.
   - On this branch, the wallet stays closed and nothing is logged. Once the cart request finishes the overlay lifts and the buttons disappear for about a second while the Element is rebuilt, then come back. That rebuild happens on every refresh today; only the grey overlay is new.
3. Tap again. The wallet opens with the refreshed total, line items, and shipping options. Complete the payment and check the order total and shipping method.
4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 with a virtual product and a coupon, so the total changes without any shipping event. The sheet must show the refreshed total.
5. On the classic cart page, change a quantity and click Update cart. Repeat the pending-refresh tap and the retry.
6. With throttling off, confirm the button still opens normally after country, postcode, shipping, and coupon changes, and that the product page and order-pay page buttons are unaffected.

Overlapping refreshes, failed refreshes, and the order-pay scoping are covered by the automated tests; no request interception is needed for the manual pass.

commit_log:
fix(express-checkout): guard the button from update_checkout on classic checkout
The guard and overlay only started at `updated_checkout`, i.e. once
WooCommerce's own `update_order_review` request had finished. Our container
hooks at `woocommerce_checkout_before_customer_details`, outside the
`.woocommerce-checkout-payment` and review-order table core greys out, so
during core's request the old button stayed tappable with `cachedCartData`
still holding the pre-change snapshot. For a virtual cart no address or
rate event ever corrects the sheet, so it would show the old total while
the server charges the new one.

Raise the guard and the overlay from `update_checkout`, which core fires
before its request; the forced refresh that follows `updated_checkout`
takes them over and releases them. Checkout context only: `init_checkout`
fires `update_checkout` on the order-pay page too, where core bails out
without a `form.checkout` and never fires `updated_checkout`, so a guard
raised there would never come down.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: <redacted>
�
feat(express-checkout): overlay the button while the cart refreshes
While WooCommerce refreshes the cart, the click guard rejects taps on the
still-mounted Element, but nothing told the shopper why a tap did nothing.
On classic checkout the container also sits outside the order-review area
core greys out, so it looked fully active during the refresh.

Block the container with the same white blockUI overlay core paints over
the order review for the duration of the forced refresh, and lift it from
the refresh that still owns the button, so a superseded refresh finishing
first cannot drop it early. `unblock()` is split out of `unblockButton()`
because `init()` has already decided whether the container belongs on
screen: only the overlay comes off. The product-page refresh's failure
path unblocks too, otherwise `blockUI.isBlocked` stays truthy and
`blockButton()` skips every later overlay.

The overlay is a signal, not the guard: an element-level blockUI block
binds no keyboard events, so the `event.reject()` guard stays in place for
keyboard and assistive-tech activation.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: <redacted>
�
refactor(express-checkout): drop the cart refresh deadline and abort
The forced cart refresh carried an AbortController, a 10 s deadline and a
`getCart({ signal })` argument, plus a third `isSuperseded()` checkpoint
right before mounting the Element.

The deadline was added to cure a hung refresh holding the click guard
forever, but the single-owner refresh already cures that: the next refresh
supersedes the hung one and its late result is discarded. What the timer
still bought was only the case where no further refresh ever happens, at
the cost of aborting a legitimately slow Store API response on a slow
network and hiding the button until the next refresh. The pre-mount
checkpoint cannot trip in production either: nothing awaits between the
post-`getStripe()` check and `mount()`.

Remove all three. The refresh owner is now a plain id, `cart-api.js` is
unchanged again, and the hung-refresh test uses a never-settling promise
instead of an abort signal. The contrived pre-mount test goes with the
checkpoint it exercised.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: <redacted>
�
fix(express-checkout): bound and supersede forced cart refreshes
`refreshExpressCheckoutElement()` counted every pending refresh and released
the count only once `init()` settled. Nothing bounded the Store API cart
request - `fetch` has no timeout of its own and no signal was passed - so a
stalled response left a count outstanding forever and every wallet click was
rejected for the rest of the page. Later healthy refreshes could not repair
it: each added and removed its own count, never the stuck one. The count also
conflated "any refresh pending" with "the current refresh pending", so a hung
refresh kept gating clicks even after a newer one had installed good data.

Track a single active refresh instead of a count. Starting one aborts the
request it supersedes and takes ownership, so the guard follows the newest
refresh rather than the slowest. The request is bounded by an
AbortController, which settles the promise and releases the guard; that path
drops the cart data, so the button hides and any click still reaching the
handler rejects rather than opening a wallet against the pre-refresh
snapshot. A later healthy refresh restores it.

Only the newest generation may publish. Ownership is rechecked after the cart
fetch, and again after `getStripe()` and immediately before mounting, since
both are awaits a newer refresh can start across and `elements` is
module-global - a late generation would otherwise remount underneath a wallet
the shopper already had open.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: <redacted>
�
fix: Reject express checkout clicks during cart refresh
Classic checkout leaves the existing Express Checkout Element mounted while a Store API cart refresh and replacement initialization are in flight. Resolving a click in that window can open a wallet against stale cart data and race callbacks across Elements instances.

Track the complete forced-refresh lifecycle and reject clicks until replacement initialization finishes. Explicitly reject missing-data clicks and cover both the guarded window and post-refresh recovery.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265
�
fix(express-checkout): keep cart data readable while a refresh is in flight
The `updated_checkout` and `updated_cart_totals` listeners cleared
`cachedCartData` synchronously and then kicked off an async re-init. The
express checkout button stays mounted and clickable for that whole window
- around 800ms on an idle local store, longer on a live one - so a shopper
tapping Apple Pay or Google Pay during it ran the click handler with no
cart data. `getOnClickOptions()` returned `undefined` and the handler threw
on `options.shippingRates`, so `event.resolve()` never ran and Stripe never
opened the payment sheet. The tap silently did nothing, and because the
throw preceded `onClickHandler()`, it never reached Tracks either.

Swap the cached cart only once the response is in, the way the
`update-button-data` action already does, and pass an explicit
`forceRefresh` so the listeners still get fresh data. Guard the click
handler against missing options too, covering the product page path where
product data is cleared before the cart fetch.

Latent since 10.0.0 (#10784), which replaced a closure parameter that was
always defined with the nullable `getOnClickOptions()` return.

Refs WOOPMNT-6265
